prospects.headline_long: UiPath just posted its first profitable year on $1.9B ARR (+12%) with agentic-AI product ARR nearing $200M - a founder-led, cash-rich (NYSE: PATH) enterprise-automation leader with a brand-new CMO, no motorsport footprint, and no automation brand anywhere on the F1 grid.
prospects.the_case: UiPath is the enterprise-automation leader pivoting hard into agentic AI - software agents that orchestrate and execute work across a company's systems. FY2026 was an inflection: its first profitable full year ($57M operating income, $282M net income), $1.9B ARR up 12%, $1.7B cash and no debt, with AI-product ARR (agentic automation, intelligent document processing, the Maestro orchestration layer) reaching ~$200M. Founder-CEO Daniel Dines is back at the helm framing the agentic-orchestration thesis, and a brand-new CMO - Michael Atalla (ex-Microsoft, ex-F5), appointed August 2025 - was hired to elevate exactly this story. No automation or agentic-AI orchestration brand sits anywhere on the F1 grid, so the category is open, and UiPath is a profitable, cash-rich company with the means to own it.
prospects.why_now: Two clocks align. First, a new CMO (Atalla, Aug 2025) is in the window when marquee brand investments get defined - and he was hired specifically to elevate UiPath's agentic-AI leadership. Second, the agentic-AI category is in a land-grab for enterprise mindshare, and UiPath's first profitable year gives it both the confidence and the balance sheet to invest in brand. The open automation lane on the grid is cheap to plant now, before a peer notices it.
prospects.why_team: McLaren is the fit: the grid's deepest enterprise-software partner roster (Dell, Salesforce, Workday, Google) means a proven hospitality machine aimed at exactly the CIO/COO/automation buyers UiPath sells to, and a premium, technology-forward brand that mirrors UiPath's 'orchestration' positioning. The automation category is uncontested there. Aston Martin (boardroom enterprise audience) and Williams (data/engineering) are documented alternatives.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A (developing) - real substance, not signage. (1) TECHNICAL/OPERATIONAL: an F1 team runs on sprawling, repetitive back-office and engineering workflows - parts procurement and logistics across a global calendar, supplier onboarding, finance and compliance ops, and data movement between simulation, telemetry and strategy systems. That is exactly what UiPath's agentic automation and orchestration layer attacks: automating and orchestrating those processes so engineers and operations staff spend time on performance, not paperwork. A defined workstream (automating the team's logistics/finance/data ops with agentic orchestration) is genuine operational value and a flagship reference deployment. (2) COMMERCIAL: McLaren's enterprise-software partner audience - the CIOs, COOs and automation buyers UiPath sells to - is exactly its market, so race-weekend hospitality becomes a working enterprise pipeline channel, with co-marketing across UiPath's large enterprise base. (3) CONTENT & TALENT: an 'automation behind a winning team' content platform and a joint engineering/AI-talent narrative. The team gains real operational efficiency plus aligned co-marketing; UiPath gains a live, referenceable deployment and a premium enterprise stage for its agentic-AI story.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Automation / Agentic AI Partner tier on McLaren, minimum three years, estimated $4-6M/yr (calibrated to $1.9B ARR and profitability), with category exclusivity for automation/agentic-AI orchestration, a working automation deployment across the team's operations, and B2B hospitality + content aimed at UiPath's enterprise buyers.

Helion just raised $465M at $15.5B with the world's first fusion power deal (Microsoft, 2028) and no motorsport footprint. The honest caveat: pre-revenue deep-tech, so this is a brand/relationship play, not a deal to force.

score_rationale.timing: Just closed a $465M Series G at a $15.5B valuation (~Jun 2026, ~3x from $5.43B in Jan 2025) and is moving publicly from lab milestone (Polaris) to construction (Orion for Microsoft) - a peak-visibility moment.
score_rationale.capacity: $15.5B valuation, $465M just raised, $1B+ cumulative - funded; tempered only by being pre-revenue (no commercial fusion until ~2028).
score_rationale.brand_fit: Fusion clean energy on the clean-mobility grid is arguably the single most on-narrative pairing available; tempered by MODE B (a halo, not in-car tech).
score_rationale.urgency: A fresh mega-round creates a brand window, but there is no competitor-on-grid clock or dated motorsport anchor.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE B: fusion does not power an FE car (batteries do), so the value is brand, narrative and talent - not an operational integration.

prospects.headline_long: Sam Altman-backed fusion pioneer Helion just raised $465M at a $15.5B valuation - nearly 3x in 18 months - with the world's first fusion power deal (Microsoft, 2028) and no motorsport footprint: the definitive clean-energy brand for Formula E's clean-mobility stage.
prospects.the_case: Helion Energy is the fusion company turning 'limitless clean power' from physics into a construction site. In June 2026 it raised a $465M Series G at a $15.5B valuation - nearly tripling from $5.43B in January 2025 - to build Orion, its first commercial plant (Malaga, WA), which will deliver 50MW to Microsoft by 2028 under the world's first fusion power-purchase agreement. In February 2026 its Polaris machine became the first privately-funded device to run on deuterium-tritium fuel and reach 150 million degrees. For 1440 the fit is narrative, not operational: fusion is the definitive clean-energy story and Formula E is the championship built to prove clean mobility, so a Helion-FE pairing is the most on-message sustainability partnership on any grid - and Helion has never touched motorsport. The honest counterweight: it is pre-revenue and pouring capital into reactors, so its near-term sponsorship appetite is the open question - a brand/relationship play to open now, not a deal to force.
prospects.why_now: Helion just closed a $465M round at a $15.5B valuation - a peak-visibility moment - and is moving publicly from lab milestone (Polaris) to construction (Orion for Microsoft, 2028). That arc is exactly when a deep-tech brand benefits from a global, on-narrative stage and a STEM-talent magnet. No clean-energy or fusion brand holds an FE position, so the on-theme lane is open and cheap to plant now.
prospects.why_team: Envision Racing is the sharpest fit: a sustainability-first independent whose entire identity ('Race Against Climate Change') mirrors Helion's clean-energy mission, with a clean (greenfield) roster so Helion can own the clean-energy lane outright. A manufacturer team (e.g. Nissan or Jaguar) is the alternative if a larger stage is preferred over thematic purity.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B - a brand, narrative and talent partnership, not in-car tech (fusion doesn't power an FE car - batteries do). The substance is real on three fronts. (1) NARRATIVE: fusion is the definitive clean-energy story and Formula E is the championship built to prove clean mobility, so pairing 'the power source of the future' with 'the racing of the future' is the most on-message sustainability partnership available on any grid - and it supercharges Envision's own 'Race Against Climate Change' identity rather than bolting a logo onto it. (2) CREDIBILITY & COMMERCIAL: Helion's profile - the world's first fusion power-purchase agreement (Microsoft), a $15.5B valuation, a Polaris machine at 150 million degrees - lends Envision a marquee deep-tech innovation halo that materially lifts a sustainability-first independent's partner roster and helps it win and keep other backers, while Helion's high-profile ecosystem opens enterprise and policy doors. (3) TALENT & CONTENT: a 'fusion meets electric racing' content platform and a STEM/engineering recruiting halo for both - Helion is hiring physicists and engineers at speed in a fierce market. Envision gains a category-defining clean-energy story, commercial lift and talent pull; Helion gains a global, on-narrative stage as it moves from lab to grid.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Clean Energy / Innovation Partner tier on Envision Racing, minimum three years, ~$2-4M/yr (calibrated to a pre-revenue deep-tech's modest near-term appetite, structured to scale toward Orion's 2028 delivery), with category exclusivity for energy/fusion and a content-and-talent programme rather than heavy signage.

prospects.the_case: AlphaSense is the AI platform for market intelligence and search across the financial and business world - the tool banks, asset managers, hedge funds and a majority of the S&P 500 use to find and trust insight. On 3 June 2026 it closed a $350M round at a ~$7.5B valuation (led by Vitruvian Partners, Accenture Ventures and J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners), nearly doubling its 2024 mark, on more than $600M of ARR. It has scale and momentum - the $930M Tegus acquisition in July 2024 folded in the leading expert-transcript library - and CEO Jack Kokko has said an IPO is a possibility. Two things make it a 1440 target: it has never touched motorsport, and no market- or financial-intelligence brand owns a position anywhere on the F1 grid, so the category is uncontested. Its audience - research, strategy and investment professionals - is exactly the premium enterprise crowd an F1 partnership reaches.
prospects.why_now: A $350M raise at a doubled, ~$7.5B valuation is the peak moment of brand-investment authority, and CEO Jack Kokko's openness to an IPO puts AlphaSense in the pre-listing window when enterprise credibility compounds most. A CMO appointed in 2024 with two IPO runs behind her is setting the brand agenda now. The market-intelligence category is uncontested there, so AlphaSense can own it outright. If McLaren's inventory is constrained, Williams (a data-led revival with a B2B-tech audience) and Aston Martin (boardroom-premium) are credible fallbacks.

AlphaSense's market and competitive intelligence serves a team's commercial and strategy functions directly: sponsor and partner prospecting, category and market analysis, and tracking the businesses a team wants in its garage. McLaren gains a genuine intelligence capability plus co-marketing to a shared enterprise audience; AlphaSense gains a premium global stage and hospitality in front of the finance and corporate buyers it sells to. prospects.thesis: A British embodied-AI champion ($8.6B, fresh off a $1.2B Series D) whose autonomous-mobility story maps onto Formula E's 'future of mobility' identity better than almost any brand - and no autonomy/mobility-AI brand is on the grid. The honest caveat: its buyers are automakers, so this is a brand/innovation/recruiting halo, not a B2B-pipeline play.

score_rationale.timing: Fresh $1.2B Series D at an $8.6B valuation (25 Feb 2026) and a 2026 London robotaxi launch - peak capital and brand momentum now.
score_rationale.capacity: $8.6B valuation, ~$1.5B raised in Feb 2026 (with Uber's milestone tranche); an FE deal is immaterial.
score_rationale.brand_fit: Autonomous-mobility AI is an unusually clean fit for Formula E's future-of-mobility identity, and a British brand suits the championship - though as MODE B the value is a halo, not in-car tech.
score_rationale.urgency: Fresh capital and a recruiting land-grab in autonomy, but no dated external forcing function.
score_rationale.ops_fit: MODE A (developing): not Wayve's product in the car, but its AI, simulation and data-science capabilities applied to the team's race-strategy, energy-modelling and simulation work - a real, deepenable technical workstream.

prospects.headline_long: Wayve - Britain's embodied-AI leader for autonomous driving, valued at $8.6B after a $1.2B Series D in February 2026 - is the rare brand whose 'future of mobility' story is native to Formula E, with no autonomy or mobility-AI brand anywhere on the grid.
prospects.the_case: Wayve is the UK's embodied-AI champion for autonomous driving: founded in 2017 by CEO Alex Kendall, it raised a $1.2B Series D in February 2026 (about $1.5B including Uber's milestone tranche) at an $8.6B valuation, backed by SoftBank, Nvidia, Microsoft and Uber alongside automakers Mercedes-Benz, Nissan and Stellantis. It is launching a London Uber robotaxi service in 2026 and supervised-autonomy software in consumer vehicles from 2027. For Formula E - the championship that exists to tell the future-of-electric-mobility story - an autonomous-mobility-AI brand is an unusually native fit, and no autonomy or mobility-AI brand holds an FE partnership. The honest counterweight: Wayve's customers are automakers, reached through industry channels, so a motorsport play is a brand, innovation-narrative and recruiting halo (it is in a fierce AI talent war), not a B2B-pipeline channel.
prospects.why_now: Wayve is freshly capitalized ($1.2B in Feb 2026) and scaling fast into commercial robotaxi launches - a brand-building inflection where a young, recruiting-hungry AI company invests in identity and talent visibility. The autonomy/mobility lane on the FE grid is empty, so moving now secures a clean, native category before a peer notices it.
prospects.why_team: Nissan Formula E fits on the merits: a works EV manufacturer with no autonomy or mobility-AI partner on its car, so Wayve owns the lane, and the deepest engineering counterpart on the grid for a real technical workstream. There is also a relationship door - Nissan is one of the automakers (with Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis) that invested in Wayve's Feb 2026 Series D - which warms an introduction and offers a ready 'showcase our autonomy bet' narrative. Treat that as a door-opener, not a near-done deal: a strategic road-car investment and an FE marketing spend are separate decisions on separate budgets - which is precisely the gap 1440 would broker. Envision Racing (a sustainability-first independent with a greenfield roster) is the clean-slate alternative.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE A (developing) - real substance on three fronts, not signage. (1) TECHNICAL: Wayve's core competencies - embodied AI, large-scale simulation, real-time perception-and-control and sensor/data fusion - map onto a works team's hardest problems: race-strategy optimisation under uncertainty, energy- and battery-management modelling across a stint, and high-fidelity simulation. A defined joint workstream (Wayve engineers paired with Nissan's strategy and simulation group) gives genuine performance value, with room to deepen over the term. (2) A SHOWCASE NARRATIVE: Nissan is among Wayve's Series-D automaker investors, so a visible partnership could turn that strategic bet into a public tech-leadership story - positioning Nissan at the front of the autonomy-plus-EV future its brand is staking out (a warm intro and a ready angle, not a deal the investment makes automatic). (3) STORY & TALENT: a shared future-of-mobility content platform plus a co-branded recruiting programme in a brutal autonomy talent market. Nissan gains performance capability, a differentiated innovation narrative and recruiting pull; Wayve gains a works-manufacturer global stage and deepens a strategic relationship.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Mobility AI Partner tier on Nissan Formula E (Envision Racing as a clean-independent alternative), minimum three years, ~$3-5M/yr, with category exclusivity for autonomy/mobility-AI, a defined joint technical workstream (Wayve AI/simulation applied to race strategy and energy modelling), and a content/innovation-narrative programme aimed at talent and enterprise audiences.

prospects.headline_long: Honeywell Aerospace becomes a standalone ~$17B-revenue public company on 29 June 2026 - a born-big aerospace pure-play with a precision-engineering F1 halo and a fresh brand-establishment mandate, but unproven motorsport-sponsorship appetite.
prospects.the_case: Honeywell is splitting into three public companies, and the final step - spinning off Honeywell Aerospace as a standalone business - distributes on 29 June 2026. The new company will have more than $17B in annual revenue and be one of the largest publicly-traded aerospace suppliers, with leading positions in propulsion, cockpit and navigation systems, and auxiliary power. Two things make it worth a conversation. First, a spin-off is a brand-establishment moment: a newly independent public company must build an identity distinct from its former parent, which is exactly when first-mover brand investments get approved. Second, aerospace precision-engineering carries a genuine F1 halo - propulsion, materials and systems engineering are the sport's own language. The honest counterweight: this is a large, established B2B/B2G supplier whose customers (airlines, OEMs, defence) are won through procurement, not paddock hospitality, so its appetite for a motorsport sponsorship is unproven. Treat this as a relationship-and-halo play to open now, not a deal to force.
prospects.why_now: The 29 June spin-off creates a finite brand-establishment window - new CEO Jim Currier and a fresh standalone leadership team will set the independent company's identity and brand-investment agenda in its first two quarters. Opening a conversation around the listing positions 1440 early, before the new entity's priorities harden, even though this is a longer-horizon relationship than a pre-IPO growth brand.
prospects.why_team: Aston Martin is the fit: premium British engineering gravitas and a boardroom, government-adjacent hospitality audience that suits an aerospace brand's enterprise and institutional buyers, positioning Honeywell Aerospace as a precision-engineering halo rather than a mass-market sponsor. The aerospace lane is distinct from Aston Martin's existing technology partners, and as a US-headquartered company an American-team alternative (Cadillac) is the documented fallback if a US-sovereignty narrative is preferred.
prospects.value_to_team: MODE B. The value is a precision-engineering brand association, an R&D/innovation narrative (materials, simulation, sensors and systems engineering are shared language between aerospace and F1), and premium hospitality - not an in-car technical integration. Aston Martin gains a blue-chip aerospace partner and an engineering-credibility story; Honeywell Aerospace gains a global stage to establish its standalone brand.

First, Murphy is roughly five months into a mandate her own company has branded a growth-phase reset - the precise window in which a new CMO defines the multi-year brand-investment agenda and shapes the next fiscal year's budget, before priorities harden. Second, because she has already delivered an F1/FE programme, the usual internal objection - 'does motorsport actually work for a B2B audience?' - is pre-answered by her personal track record, collapsing the normal 12-18 month education cycle to near zero. Third, the category whitespace is a depreciating asset: the moment a DevSecOps rival (Sonatype, Snyk or GitLab) plants a flag, JFrog's first-mover narrative is gone and the conversation becomes a defensive one. Moving in the next 4-6 weeks captures all three.

If McLaren's relevant inventory is constrained, Aston Martin is the strong fallback: it carries premium enterprise gravitas, its hospitality audience skews to exactly the CISO and CTO buyers JFrog sells to, and its technology-partner roster leaves the DevSecOps slot open. A deal can therefore be structured around a real integration into the team's engineering workflow, giving McLaren an authentic 'official software supply chain partner' story it can stand behind technically, plus a credible R&D narrative, plus enterprise hospitality where JFrog's own buyers already gather on race weekends. The team gains tooling and a reference customer; JFrog gains a live proof point and a stage.

The 'physical AI / autonomy' lane is unclaimed today, which rewards a first mover before the generic-AI deals expand to crowd it. Haas gets a high-credibility, deep-pocketed partner and aligned co-marketing; Applied Intuition gets a premium B2B stage in front of its exact buyers ahead of an IPO.

prospects.headline_long: Fairmat - the French deep-tech turning carbon-fibre waste into new structural composite (FairPly) - has never been in motorsport, and for a team that builds its own carbon-fibre F1 car it is a real, two-way sustainability-and-materials partnership, not a logo.
prospects.the_case: Fairmat (Paris, founded 2020) uses a patented cold-atmospheric-plasma process to recycle aerospace and wind carbon-fibre waste into FairPly, a new structural composite - closing the loop on a material that is otherwise landfilled or burned. It raised a EUR51.5M Series B in Apr 2025 (EUR26.5M equity + EUR25M EIB venture debt; Bpifrance and Slate VC leading, with Temasek, Pictet, Singular, CNP and Infinity Recycling), ~$114M in total, and already sells to Hexcel, Siemens Gamesa and sports brands (Decathlon, DPS Skis). It has never touched motorsport. The fit is with F1, not FE, for a concrete reason: FE uses a spec chassis (Spark builds the common monocoque for all teams), so recycled composite there is a championship-level choice - whereas an F1 constructor designs and manufactures its OWN carbon-fibre car (~85% of it composite), so Fairmat is a genuine team-level materials workstream and a direct lever on F1's Net Zero 2030 pledge. HONEST framing: near-term use is non-structural/bodywork, garage and facility composites plus verified sustainability data, co-developing toward structural parts (homologation makes fully-structural longer-dated) - so it is a WARM, real-but-scaling MODE-A. Decision-maker: Founder & CEO Benjamin Saada.
prospects.why_now: F1's Net Zero 2030 commitment and the cost cap are pushing teams toward sustainable, lower-cost materials now, and Fairmat is scaling post-Series-B with FairPly in commercial demand - so a founding materials relationship is best built early, before a rival team or composite brand claims the 'recycled carbon fibre' position. The honest why-now is positional, not a dated trigger.
prospects.why_team: Williams is an engineering-revival constructor that designs and builds its own carbon-fibre car, with a materials/sustainability lane that is open (its Atlassian, VAST, Keeper and Anthropic deals are all non-materials), so a recycled-composite partner is a genuine engineering and Net-Zero story rather than a logo - and a right-sized, mutual innovation partnership for a midfield team using material smarts to punch up. No partner conflict (Fairmat's backers are diversified funds, none a Williams rival).
prospects.value_to_team: A TWO-WAY exchange (tech + business both directions), not sponsorship cash - three concrete swaps. (1) MATERIAL <-> PROVING GROUND: Fairmat supplies FairPly recycled carbon fibre for the team's composite parts (bodywork, garage/transport and facility structures, co-developing toward more), cutting material cost and footprint; in return the F1 car - the most extreme structural test on earth - becomes Fairmat's ultimate performance validation and global reference, de-risking FairPly for its aerospace/auto buyers. (2) SUSTAINABILITY DATA <-> CREDIBILITY: Fairmat gives the team auditable recycled-content and CO2-avoided data that feeds its FIA / F1 Net-Zero-2030 reporting and a real (non-greenwash) circular-materials story; the team gives Fairmat a global sustainability-leadership stage and a marquee engineering brand association. (3) CO-ENGINEERING R&D <-> BUYER NETWORK: joint R&D subjecting recycled composite to F1 loads advances FairPly's spec and IP; the team's paddock and its OEM/aerospace ecosystem open exactly the industrial composite buyers (the Hexcel/Siemens-Gamesa world) Fairmat needs to scale. Williams gets cost-down sustainable material + a hard ESG story; Fairmat gets validation, a stage and buyers.
prospects.deal_architecture: Official Sustainable-Materials / Recycled-Composite Partner on Williams, minimum three years, ~$2-4M/yr (right-sized to a scale-up), structured as a co-development + material-supply workstream (non-structural and facility composites first, structural R&D roadmap) plus a joint Net-Zero-2030 sustainability-data and content programme - value exchanged both ways, not a pure logo fee.
